method: Each entry is an independent check of the stored expected value in evals/benchmark_phase2.json or evals/conversation_phase3.json. 'sql' entries are hand-written DuckDB SQL executed directly on the parquet views — they never call the planner (no plan(), no build_sql()). Scalar/breakdown/series SQL is re-derived from catalog/measures.yaml and sql/canonical_metrics.sql (the documented definitions), with app/country/platform filters written out by hand where the case is scoped. 'weather' entries recompute report cards directly from the raw tables using the period definitions documented in src/socialpulse_nlq/weather.py (current = last 28 days of sessions, prior = the 28 days before; retention cohorts end at max-date minus 7 days). The oracle runner first asserts MAX(session date) = 2026-03-31, so the hardcoded periods fail loudly if the data ever changes. 'behavioral' entries check the premise of a clarification/refusal against the data or registry instead of against the planner. 'registry' entries read catalog/experiments.yaml directly. The oracle NEVER compares SQL text: agreement is always on executed values. Where the oracle disagrees with a stored expected value, the stored value is NOT changed — the disagreement is reported as a finding.
